# TROUBLESHOOTING.md

Symptom-first index of known issues. Each links to the fuller writeup in
[DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) where relevant.

---

### `406 Not Acceptable` / "This error was generated by Mod_Security"

The maat.ae server runs ModSecurity, which blocks two specific things we've
found so far:

1. **The default `python-requests` User-Agent.** Fixed by
   `app/woocommerce.py::BROWSER_HEADERS`, applied to every WooCommerce and
   WordPress request. If you write a new HTTP call anywhere in this codebase,
   reuse `BROWSER_HEADERS` — don't call `requests.get/post` with default headers.
2. **The literal `Content-Type: image/webp` header value** on media uploads,
   regardless of actual file content. Fixed in `app/wordpress_media.py` by
   always sending `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and letting
   WordPress infer the real type from the filename.

If you hit a *new* 406 somewhere else, assume it's ModSecurity blocking on some
header value again — isolate by changing one header at a time (User-Agent,
Content-Type, Accept), the same way both of the above were found. See
[DECISIONS.md #2](DECISIONS.md#2-modsecurity-blocks-the-default-python-requests-user-agent)
and [#10](DECISIONS.md#10-modsecurity-also-blocks-the-imagewebp-content-type-header-specifically).

### A published product got the wrong id/link, or WooCommerce returns a *list* when you expected one object

Almost certainly `WC_URL` doesn't match the site's canonical domain form (e.g.
`www` vs non-www), causing a 301 redirect that silently downgrades the POST to a
GET. Check `WC_URL` in `.env` matches exactly. The code now raises explicitly on
a 301/302 instead of following it — if you see that raised error, this is the
fix. Full story: [DECISIONS.md #1](DECISIONS.md#1-woocommerce-post-silently-returned-the-wrong-product).

### `401 rest_cannot_create` — "Sorry, you are not allowed to create posts as this user" on `wp/v2/media`

You're using `WC_CK`/`WC_CS` (WooCommerce keys) for a WordPress core endpoint.
Media uploads need `WP_USERNAME`/`WP_APP_PASSWORD` instead. See
[DECISIONS.md #9](DECISIONS.md#9-wordpress-media-uploads-need-a-different-credential-from-woocommerce).

---

### `401 invalid_username` or `401 incorrect_password` on WordPress auth

`WP_USERNAME` is wrong. Common mistakes, both hit during this project's own
setup:
- Using the **display name** shown in wp-admin instead of the login username
  (they can differ — but sometimes a site's actual username *is* the full name,
  e.g. `"Mishaal Rahman"` with a space, which is legal in WordPress even though
  unusual).
- Using the **label** you typed when creating the Application Password (e.g.
  `"Fihris-Agent"`) — that's just a name for the password, not a username.

To find the real login username with certainty:

```bash
python -c "
import requests
from requests.auth import HTTPBasicAuth
from app.config import settings
from app.woocommerce import BROWSER_HEADERS
auth = HTTPBasicAuth(settings.WP_USERNAME, settings.WP_APP_PASSWORD)
r = requests.get(f'{settings.WC_URL}/wp-json/wp/v2/users/me', headers=BROWSER_HEADERS, auth=auth)
print(r.status_code, r.text[:300])
"
```

`200` with your account details confirms both values are correct. Don't
brute-force-guess usernames against a live site — some security plugins
(Wordfence etc.) ban an IP after repeated failed logins.

### `WooCommerce API returned error: ...Error getting remote image...`

The `image_url` you supplied doesn't resolve (404, DNS failure, etc.) —
WooCommerce tries to sideload the image server-side and fails. Check the URL
loads in a browser first. Also affects the example payload in
`app/schemas.py`/Swagger docs if it's ever left pointing at a stale URL.

### Gemini `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` / quota errors

Free-tier Gemini API keys have a **per-model daily quota** (as low as 20
requests/day on some models). `app/gemini.py::MODELS_TO_TRY` already falls back
through `gemini-3.7-flash` → `gemini-3.5-flash` → `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, so a
quota hit on one model shouldn't fail the whole request — but if *all three* are
exhausted, generation will fail outright. This is an external quota limit, not a
code bug; either wait for the daily reset or use a paid-tier key.

Note the retry loop (`MAX_WRITER_ATTEMPTS = 5`) tries the model list from the
top on *every* writer attempt — if the first model in the list is
quota-exhausted, each retry wastes a few seconds hitting it before falling
through. This is expected, not a hang.

### `422` "Could not produce a listing that passes SEO validation"

Not necessarily a bug — the writer/validator loop exhausted 5 attempts. The
`detail` message includes the *exact* last set of failing rules (e.g. "Keyphrase
density too high", "no seo_title was generated"). Read it before assuming
something is broken. Common real causes:
- `raw_specs` too thin to naturally reach ~350 words without stuffing
- A focus keyphrase that's awkward to repeat naturally (very long, or a strange
  phrase) — triggers density/distribution failures
- Occasionally a single Gemini response is malformed (missing the newer JSON
  fields) — a genuinely bad generation, not a validator bug; it should self-correct
  on the next attempt

If you suspect the *validator* itself is wrong (not the generated content), test
it in isolation against a hand-crafted state per
[SETUP.md](SETUP.md#verifying-your-setup-without-publishing-anything) rather
than debugging through a full live Gemini+WooCommerce round trip.

---

### Frontend keeps running an old version of `main.js`/`categories.js`/etc. after a reload

Should no longer happen — `main.py` sends `Cache-Control: no-store` on `/upload`
and everything under `/upload-assets/*` specifically to prevent this. If you
still see it, check the response headers (`curl -sI http://localhost:8000/upload-assets/js/<file>.js`)
to confirm that middleware is actually running, and check the browser's dev
tools Network tab isn't set to "Disable cache" being the *only* thing keeping
it fresh (i.e. confirm it's fresh with dev tools closed too). Full story:
[DECISIONS.md #16](DECISIONS.md#16-frontend-static-assets-served-with-cache-control-no-store).

### I created test data on the live store while debugging

It happens — image uploads and product creation both have real, immediate
side effects on production. Clean up via the REST API:

```bash
# Delete a test media item
python -c "
import requests
from requests.auth import HTTPBasicAuth
from app.config import settings
from app.woocommerce import BROWSER_HEADERS
auth = HTTPBasicAuth(settings.WP_USERNAME, settings.WP_APP_PASSWORD)
requests.delete(f'{settings.WC_URL}/wp-json/wp/v2/media/<ID>',
    params={'force': 'true'}, headers=BROWSER_HEADERS, auth=auth)
"
```

See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the rule this is trying to prevent in the first
place: confirm with a human before any call that publishes/uploads for real.
